probes.code: function parseDecimal(raw) { if (raw == null || String(raw).trim() === '') return { ok: false, error: 'empty' }; const value = Number(raw); return Number.isFinite(value) ? { ok: true, value } : { ok: false, error: 'invalid-number' }; } function calculate(a, operator, b) { if (!['+', '-'].includes(operator)) return { ok: false, error: 'unsupported-operator' }; return { ok: true, value: operator === '+' ? a + b : a - b }; } class Calculator { calculate(a, operator, b) { return calculate(a, operator, b); } } const values = ['12.5', ' ', '12px', 'Infinity'].map(parseDecimal); console.log(JSON.stringify({ values, functionResult: calculate(7, '-', 2), classResult: new Calculator().calculate(7, '-', 2), badOperator: calculate(1, '*', 2) }));

excerpts.text: Calling Number as a function converts the supplied value to a Number according to the specification conversion rules.
Number.isFinite returns false for non-Number values and for NaN or positive or negative infinity.
